profiles.meeting_scenario: A design review meeting at a quantitative trading firm to evaluate a draft proposal for moving a Genetic Programming research pipeline into the firm's pilot-trading stack. The design covers evolving intraday USD/JPY strategies from 5-minute OHLC inputs for AUD/USD, EUR/USD, GBP/USD, and USD/JPY, comparing training-only versus validation-assisted candidate selection, and packaging the chosen strategy into a limited paper-trading deployment. The agenda is to review whether the current design note is complete enough for conditional approval, with particular attention to multi-instrument data handling, what must be retained from the validation-selection process, how the standard pilot deployment template applies, and how success in the out-of-sample period is being defined. The expected outcome is agreement on a short revision list and a go/no-go recommendation for implementation handoff.

members.name: Nadia Chen
members.expertise: Genetic programming, FX alpha research, walk-forward evaluation
members.background: Nadia leads the firm's exploratory systematic FX research pod and has a background in academic-style symbolic strategy discovery, especially free-form rule generation from multi-instrument market data.
members.private_state: She wants the review to end with quick approval for a paper-trading pilot and is trying to preserve the published research protocol with as little implementation-driven redesign as possible.
hidden_assumptions: When a design note says the four FX pairs use the same 5-minute OHLC bars, that already implies the firm's historical preprocessing has row-aligned them on a canonical bar grid suitable for direct ingestion.

Saving the validation-selected strategies means persisting the final chosen strategy expression and its headline backtest statistics for each run, because that is the artifact needed to reproduce the reported comparison.

Using the standard pilot deployment template means wrapping the research signal generator in the lightweight sandbox service the quant team has used for prior paper-trading trials, with basic monitoring and kill-switch hooks.

Defining success in the out-of-sample period means judging whether the held-out historical test block preserves trade activity, accuracy, and profitability characteristics similar to the training-era findings.

If transaction costs and execution assumptions are not called out in the review, the desk's usual backtest conventions are understood to carry over unless someone explicitly proposes a different template.

members.name: Owen Patel
members.expertise: Market data systems, research-to-production controls, automated FX execution infrastructure
members.background: Owen designs the firm's deployment framework for systematic strategies and has spent years translating quantitative prototypes into auditable services that behave consistently across backtest, replay, and live environments.
members.private_state: He wants to prevent a superficially approved design from later failing implementation review, so he is quietly steering the discussion toward operational completeness without sounding like he is blocking research.
hidden_assumptions: If multiple instruments are consumed on 5-minute bars, the design must specify how bar-close alignment, missing ticks, and late updates are handled so every input reflects only what was knowable at that timestamp.

Saving the validation-selected strategies means retaining the full lineage needed for governance and replay, including per-run candidate identities, validation ranking outputs, and enough metadata to reconstruct why a candidate was selected.

Using the standard pilot deployment template means inheriting the firm's normal deployable-service contract, including explicit replay behavior, broker-session handling, reconnect logic, and named execution configuration, only with lower capital and stricter safety limits.

Defining success in the out-of-sample period means establishing the KPI thresholds and reporting shape that the upcoming paper-trading window will be judged against, not just citing historical holdout results.
Any omission around costs, fills, or FX conversion treatment is a gap in the design rather than an implicit default, because deployment templates are selected and versioned explicitly.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the same 5-minute bars across instruments
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to feeding the GP engine the four pairs on the same 5-minute OHLC bars
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes the firm's standard historical preprocessing has already produced a canonical row-aligned bar matrix for AUD/USD, EUR/USD, GBP/USD, and USD/JPY, so the engine can simply read synchronized rows.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes the implementation must explicitly define timestamp alignment, bar-close semantics, and missing/late data handling so that replay and live service use only information available at each decision point.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In a quant research setting, 'same 5-minute bars' sounds like routine shorthand for synchronized inputs, so both hear a competent shared premise rather than a hidden difference in execution procedure.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to save the validation-selected strategies
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the validation-selected strategies should be saved for review and handoff
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means saving the final selected strategy formula from each GP run, along with summary backtest outputs used in the research comparison.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means saving the broader artifact set behind selection, including candidate identifiers, validation ranking traces, and enough metadata to reconstruct the selection lineage during governance review.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'save the validation-selected strategies' naturally sounds complete to both sides, and because each imagines a reasonable artifact package, neither feels a need to unpack exactly how much selection context is included.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in the standard pilot deployment template
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss putting the strategy into the standard pilot deployment template
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks the standard pilot deployment template is the lightweight research sandbox wrapper used for paper-trading trials, mainly requiring signal scheduling, basic monitoring, and kill-switch support.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks the standard pilot deployment template is the firm's normal deployable service pattern applied at pilot scale, which still requires explicit reconnect behavior, replay consistency, execution configuration, and operational ownership fields.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Because both have internal reasons to treat 'standard pilot deployment template' as a familiar existing object, the phrase creates false consensus even though each is invoking a different level of operational completeness.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to define success in the out-of-sample period
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the design should define success in the out-of-sample period before the pilot proceeds
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means success should be grounded in the historical held-out test block already shown in the design note, where stability of activity, accuracy, and profitability characteristics can be assessed.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means success should be specified as KPI thresholds for the upcoming paper-trading period, since that is the operational out-of-sample stage the pilot will actually be judged on.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The term 'out-of-sample period' is standard in both research and deployment conversations, and each interpretation feels locally obvious enough that neither participant expects the other to be referring to a different evaluation window.
